title: First-Class Appendices for Print Reports and Zwischenbericht Anhänge
description: Add first-class appendix support to the semio print system (print/tex/): an appendix is a document attached to the main report, behaving like a chapter — numbered A, B, C…, labeled Anhang/Appendix, TOC entry, chip styling, cross-referenceable via \appendixref, listed via \listofappendices. Fix a pre-existing bug where window registers (\listoffigures etc.) render header-only because semio@render@register reads the wrong body macro. Wire the feature into all six print templates (report, paper, flyer n/a, zukunftbau forschungsbericht/zwischenbericht/kompaktbericht). Then apply it to mit-bestand/bericht/zwischenbericht/zwischenbericht.tex: convert 9 Anhang markdown documents from temp/ into 8 LaTeX appendices (A-H), including a 67-project table with per-row avatar images sourced from temp/projekt_bilder/ (downscaled ~600px, copied into zwischenbericht/asset/projekt/). Update body cross-references to use \appendixref. Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/print-reports-should-be-joyful-haven.md.
summary:
Fixed the reported image overshoot: several project photos (first confirmed case: P.K.4 "KA13 / Kristian Augusts gate 13") were bleeding past the right edge of their "Bild" window into the "Allgemein" table next to it.

Root-caused it through a sequence of isolated tectonic reproductions rather than guessing: ruled out a cross-project state leak (a single image alone in its own document, on its own page, still overflowed — same failure, fully isolated) and confirmed it's specific to `image-fit=cover` combined with a strongly-portrait image (KA13 is 386×600px, aspect 0.64) rendered into a landscape-shaped target box. Added temporary debug output to `\semio_image_typeset_cover:n` (semio-window.sty) to inspect the actual computed natural/target dimensions, verified the trim/crop math by hand against those numbers, and confirmed the "crop top/bottom, output width=target_w" branch is the one exercised here — the same branch that, per a repo-wide grep, no *other* usage of `image-fit=cover` in this codebase actually exercises (every existing example uses roughly landscape source images in landscape-ish boxes), which is why this bug was never hit before. Removed the debug output once the diagnosis was confirmed; did not attempt a deeper fix to the shared `cover` trim math itself given the scope and risk of touching print-system code used elsewhere.

Fixed by switching all 67 project photos in anhang/projekte.tex from `image-fit=cover` to `image-fit=contain` — guarantees the image always stays fully inside its box (worst case some letterboxing for strongly portrait/landscape mismatches, never an overflow), and is actually closer to how the original band-row thumbnails behaved before this session's restructuring (plain `\includegraphics[height=...]`, no forced crop).

Verified: rebuilt the zwischenbericht clean (zero errors, zero unresolved refs), re-confirmed the originally-broken KA13 case now renders fully bounded with no overlap, and visually swept ~20 more catalog pages (every project from Recypark Demets through Woongroep Boschgaard) — no overshoot on any of them.
